title: arXiv physics daily — Fri, 13 Nov 2026
global_caveat: arXiv provides no official trending chart. This is an inferred ranking of notable papers, not a popularity measure; the papers are less than a day old at snapshot, so citation evidence is sparse.

sections.title: Observation of the Λ(1520) suppression in Pb-Pb collisions at √sNN = 5.02 TeV
sections.abstract: ALICE measures a 6.8σ central-to-peripheral suppression of the Λ(1520)/Λ yield ratio in Pb-Pb collisions and compares the centrality trend with hadronic-transport and statistical-hadronization models.
sections.claimed_result: Authors report a suppression fraction of 0.589 ± 0.015 stat ± 0.086 syst (about 59%; equivalent central/peripheral ratio 0.411); MUSIC+SMASH reproduces the centrality dependence.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; ALICE Pb-Pb data at √sNN=5.02 TeV across six centrality classes, with model comparisons
sections.unique_caveat: Late-stage rescattering is inferred through model comparison rather than isolated experimentally; peripheral model discrepancies remain.

sections.title: Inter-city 18.9 km free-space QKD over a dense urban corridor
sections.abstract: A decoy-state BB84 system is field-tested across an 18.9 km urban Barcelona free-space link, with measured channel parameters implying a finite-size key rate above 11 kbit/s.
sections.claimed_result: A 40-minute run had mean QBER 1.31% and approximately 19 dB average attenuation; authors estimate a finite-size secret-key rate exceeding 11 kbit/s from these measured channel parameters.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; 785 nm decoy-state BB84 over a Barcelona metropolitan free-space link
sections.unique_caveat: The secret-key rate is estimated from measured channel parameters, not demonstrated sustained fresh-key delivery; long-term unattended and day/night operation remains future work.

sections.title: A deployed four-city entanglement-based QKD network with real-time key delivery, benchmarked against finite-key security bounds
sections.abstract: The authors describe a deployed entanglement-based fiber QKD segment connecting four Slovak cities and report real-time post-processed keys on simultaneously operated links.
sections.claimed_result: Authors report 13.5 bit/s over 109 km and 4.3 bit/s over 32.1 dB loss; error correction is projected to improve finite-key rates by 4.1–6.6 times.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; entangled photons routed over deployed Slovak telecom fiber with real-time key delivery and finite-key analysis
sections.unique_caveat: The implemented heuristic privacy amplification can exceed the finite-key bound; rates depend on security analysis and post-processing choices.

sections.title: Observation of Genuine Multi-Time Quantum Memory
sections.abstract: The authors derive a three-time witness for quantum memory that evades pairwise tests and demonstrate the hierarchy in a time-continuous superconducting-qubit experiment.
sections.claimed_result: A three-time joint test detects quantum memory in a minimal qubit example where every pair of times admits a classical-memory explanation.
sections.evidence_type: experimental and theoretical; analytical witness plus a time-continuous superconducting-qubit realization with time-independent couplings
sections.unique_caveat: The demonstration is a minimal qubit implementation; broader robustness and scaling to complex environments are not established by the abstract.

sections.title: Lurkers at the Threshold: GWTC-4.0's near-threshold events
sections.abstract: The authors reanalyse 42 GWTC-4.0 candidates below the catalogue's parameter-estimation threshold, validate 29, and release posterior results for possible astrophysical candidates.
sections.claimed_result: Twenty-nine candidates pass validation; inferred spin parameters are generally weakly constrained, with several candidate signals highlighted for further analysis.
sections.evidence_type: computational; catalogue-style parameter estimation on public GWTC-4.0 strain data with automated posterior validation
sections.unique_caveat: Some candidates are consistent with noise or affected by instrumental artifacts; spin and precession hints need further robustness analysis.

sections.title: New measurement of BR(K+→π+νν̄) at the NA62 experiment
authors: Silvia Martellotti on behalf of NA62 Collaboration
sections.abstract: NA62 presents an updated K+→π+νν̄ branching-ratio analysis based on its 2023–2024 data, doubling its total dataset and expected to reach 5σ sensitivity to the Standard Model process.
sections.claimed_result: Authors report a doubled dataset and an expected 5σ sensitivity for the Standard Model process; the abstract gives no measured branching-ratio value.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; NA62 data collected at the CERN SPS, presented as a conference contribution
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract provides no branching-ratio central value, uncertainty, or observed significance; expected sensitivity is not a discovery or completed 5σ observation.

sections.title: Three-body dynamics of the Roper resonance
sections.abstract: A unitary coupled-channel amplitude including ππN dynamics is used to determine Roper resonance poles near the complex πΔ threshold.
sections.claimed_result: Fitting the P11 amplitude to SAID data with strict two- and three-body unitarity, authors report a Roper pole at √sR=1346±2+6−3−i(81±2+7−8) MeV.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; unitary coupled-channel amplitude fitted to experimental two-body amplitudes and SAID P11 data
sections.unique_caveat: The pole has parametrization-dependent systematic uncertainty; it is proposed as input for future lattice-QCD determinations, not a direct lattice observation.

sections.title: NΩ Dibaryon near Unitarity from Physical-Point Lattice QCD
sections.abstract: A physical-point lattice-QCD calculation finds an attractive NΩ interaction compatible with a shallow near-unitary dibaryon state and estimates its binding energy.
sections.claimed_result: HAL QCD analysis gives BnΩ=0.61 MeV with two uncertainty components; including finite-size Coulomb attraction gives BpΩ=1.25 MeV, also with two uncertainty components.
sections.evidence_type: computational; (2+1)-flavor lattice QCD at physical quark masses (mπ≈137 MeV) using the HAL QCD method
sections.unique_caveat: Shallow binding estimates have substantial uncertainty and depend on lattice interaction extraction; authors call for future femtoscopy and dibaryon searches.

sections.title: Rapid Multiparameter Gravitational-Wave Tests of General Relativity with Neural Posterior Estimation
sections.abstract: DINGO-TGR combines neural posterior estimation, importance sampling, and PCA to accelerate joint inference of binary parameters and six post-Newtonian deviations in GR tests.
sections.claimed_result: For GW150914, the leading-mode offset has an empirical upper-tail p-value of 11.5% in 1,000 GR-like simulations and does not reject the adopted GR null at 5% significance.
sections.evidence_type: computational; waveform inference, injection validation, and GW150914/GW250114 analyses
sections.unique_caveat: The significance calibration uses Gaussian-noise realizations and fixed detector PSDs; robustness to broader noise and waveform systematics remains open.

sections.title: Efficient Standard Siren Cosmological Inference with Posterior Reuse
sections.abstract: ASPIRE reuses posterior samples to update dark-siren cosmology and population inferences under changed assumptions, recovering nested-sampling-consistent posteriors with reported 6–28× speedups.
sections.claimed_result: Authors report posterior agreement with nested sampling and 6–28× performance improvement when reusing an existing posterior.
sections.evidence_type: computational; normalizing flows plus sequential Monte Carlo applied to dark-siren GWTC-5.0 analyses
sections.unique_caveat: Results remain conditional on source-population, galaxy-catalogue, and detection-selection assumptions; posterior reuse accelerates but does not remove them.
